title: Chicken Tikka
subtitle: Yoghurt-marinated chicken pieces grilled until charred
excerpt: Chicken pieces marinated overnight in spiced yoghurt, then cooked at high heat until charred at the edges and juicy within. The foundation of the most popular British-Indian dish and excellent in its own right.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chicken tikka is a tandoor-cooked dish with roots in Punjabi cooking, where pieces of chicken are marinated in spiced yoghurt and cooked in a clay tandoor oven at very high temperatures. The word tikka comes from a Turkic word meaning 'piece' or 'chunk'. The dish was popularised in the UK through Indian restaurants and became the base for chicken tikka masala. Without a tandoor, the key is to use the highest heat available: grill, very hot oven, or griddle pan, all work to create the characteristic char.

recipeTools.notes: Or cook under a very hot grill or on an outdoor barbecue.

content.text: Marinate for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight: the yoghurt tenderises the chicken and the spices penetrate further with more time. Score the thicker pieces of chicken deeply before marinating so the marinade reaches the centre. Shake off excess marinade before cooking: too much marinade on the surface will steam the chicken rather than char it. The chicken needs high direct heat to char quickly without drying out.

items.preparation: boneless, skinless, cut into 4 cm chunks

content.text: Combine the yoghurt, lemon juice, garlic, ginger, all the spices, oil, and salt in a large bowl. Add the chicken pieces and mix to coat thoroughly. Score any thicker pieces. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.

Remove the chicken from the fridge 20 minutes before cooking. Shake off excess marinade. Heat a griddle pan to high heat. Cook the chicken in batches for 5 to 6 minutes per side until charred in places and cooked through. Alternatively, place on a foil-lined baking tray and grill under a very hot grill for 8 to 10 minutes, turning once.
Rest for 5 minutes. Serve with fresh coriander, lemon wedges, and either naan with mint yoghurt as a starter, or with pilaf rice and a salad as a main course.
